subject: ACME Health — private fleet micropatch proposal and rollback choreography
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Micropatch proposal for private fleet (ACME) — request for approval

Alex — quick summary: we validated the hotfix for the KV cache regression and would like to run a narrow micropatch against your private fleet during the upcoming maintenance window. Major points:  
- Patch size: single binary + config delta (no model re-pinning required).
- Target: 3 customer clusters (east-us-prod, east-us-staging, east-us-canary).
- Expected service impact: rolling restart per cluster; we estimate 3–6 minutes token-serving interruption per node during drain.

Request: please confirm the maintenance windows below and whether ACME ops wants the canary to run for 24h or 72h. We will provide a preflight with telemetry and an automated rollback if error rates exceed thresholds.

Proposed windows (your local times):
- Staging: 2026-06-12 01:00–04:00 UTC
- Canary: 2026-06-12 05:00–08:00 UTC
- Prod tranche A: 2026-06-13 02:00–06:00 UTC

Attached is the proposed maintenance runbook (maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf) and a short rollback snippet. If you approve, Karthik will kick off scheduling and Soojin will own telemetry gates.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micropatch proposal for private fleet (ACME) — request for approval

Naomi — thanks for the heads-up. Staging window works. For canary we'd prefer 72h if telemetry overhead is acceptable; our compliance team wants the extended observation period for high-severity fixes. A couple of asks:  
1) Can you confirm whether service account keys rotate as part of the patch? We need to update our internal secrets rotation schedule.
2) If rollback happens, will the KV cache warm-up require degraded throughput for more than 2 hours? Our SLAs are sensitive to that.

We also need the full list of node hostnames that will be touched so our network team can monitor during the drain.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Ops, ACME Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micropatch proposal for private fleet (ACME) — request for approval

Alex — answers inline:  
1) No service-account key rotation in this micropatch. We only change runtime binary + small knobs in the config. Key rotation would be a separate, scheduled maintenance.
2) Our rollback plan includes an immediate revert to the previous binary and an automated KV cache warm-start script that preloads hot prefixes. In our lab sim the warm-up completed within ~22 minutes for a 2-node pool; in worst-case degraded-throughput mode we saw 90 minutes of above-baseline latency for large sequences. We will add a hard SLA-safe throttle to maintain 50% throughput during warm-up if you prefer.

Hostnames: I've attached a scrubbed list (we'll share full hostnames over the secure portal). For scheduling I'll put the exact hostnames in the runbook link.

Soojin will follow up with the telemetry gating thresholds and the automation play.

Best,
Naomi

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 06:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micropatch proposal for private fleet (ACME) — telemetry gates and canary plan

Hi all — telemetry gating plan below (short):
- Canary duration: 72h as requested.
- Primary gates: error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5% sustained for 10m, tail latency p95 > baseline + 40%, user-facing token-drop events > 0.2% of requests.
- Secondary gates: KV miss rate spike > 2x baseline, memory pressure > 80% on more than two nodes.
- Automated actions:
  1) If a primary gate trips, we pause rollout and run targeted diagnostic fetchers on affected pods.
  2) If errors persist after 20 minutes, automated rollback starts with node-by-node revert and cache warm-start.
  3) Post-rollback, we run a controlled traffic ramp to confirm recovery for at least 30 minutes before resuming normal traffic.

I've attached the canary results from our dry-run (canary_results_2026-06-12.csv). Observed: small error spike during drain but recovered within 7 minutes; KV warm-up completed in ~18 minutes. We will run one last dry-run in staging two nights before prod tranche.

Soojin
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micropatch proposal for private fleet (ACME) — schedule and ops ask

Alex — following up to confirm approvals and next steps:
1) Canary: 72h approved per your ask; staging dry-run scheduled 2026-06-11 23:30 UTC (night-before).
2) Prod tranche A: scheduled 2026-06-13 02:00–06:00 UTC. We'll target gradual node drain (max 10% of capacity concurrently) and a health check holdpoint after each host.
3) Rollback checklist (short):
   - Trigger: primary gate or explicit human abort.
   - Action: automated revert via fleet-manager to previous binary -> trigger cache warm-start -> throttle outgoing traffic to 50% if p95 > threshold.
   - Post-rollback verification: 30m steady-state metrics, manual sign-off from ACME ops.

Ops ask for ACME: please have a 24/7 on-call for the canary period and a single escalation contact for rapid sign-off on rollback (name + mobile number). Also confirm whether your network team wants to perform a packet-capture on the first two node drains (we can coordinate a pre-signed SCP to your monitoring bucket).

If no blockers I will formally create the change in INF-4821 and invite ACME ops to the change window.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Private Deployments
